sample_data.reset_instructions: Refresh the browser page to clear the in-memory state and reload the base JSON fixture.

problem_solving_method: A completely serverless SPA utilizing Vite and React, running 100% on the client to calculate vehicle service dates dynamically by analyzing daily run rate history, ensuring zero server-side build failures.

R1.evidence: Pre-loaded via P09_vehicle_service_public.json and parsed into memory in app.jsx

R2.evidence: engine.js calculation engine and visualised across all UI views in app.jsx

R3.evidence: Daily Call List UI component on the landing page

R4.evidence: Vehicle Detail UI component at the #/vehicle/:id route

team_members.major_contribution: Lead front-end development, orchestrated the migration to Vite for robust build tooling, designed the Premium Glassmorphic UI using Tailwind and Framer Motion, and managed AI-assisted integrations.
Architected the core prediction engine in JavaScript, implemented robust timezone and date arithmetic, and hardened algorithms against edge cases like missing data and negative running rates.

major_design_decisions: Vite + React Architecture to robustly support advanced animation libraries (Framer Motion) and complex CSS imports for the Premium Glassmorphic UI overhaul.
Pure Date Arithmetic & TZ Handling. Dates are parsed to local midnight rather than UTC constructors, preventing daylight saving shifts from affecting due dates.
known_limitations: The application uses in-memory state mapping. Recorded services or odometer updates will successfully update the UI dynamically but will not persist if the browser window is refreshed.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Rapid UI iteration, Premium Glassmorphic design, debugging Vite build/deployment issues.
